newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end flat after Canada fiscal update.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end flat after Canada fiscal update.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended flat after Canada's 1995/96 budget update on Wednesday, but market analysts expect equities to get a boost from the country's improving finances.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 0.41 point to close at 5436.13 in heavy turnover of 100.3 million shares valued at C$1.6 billion ($1.2 billion).
In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average sank 36.15 points to finish around 5930.
"By and large investors are greeting Martin's speech positively and recognize that there may be another rate reduction in Canada," said John Ing, president of Maison Placements Canada Inc.
Earlier today, Finance Minister Paul Martin confirmed market expectations that the government beat its C$32.7 billion ($24 billion) deficit target for fiscal 1995-96 ended March 31.
Martin said the 1995-96 deficit came in at C$28.6 billion ($21 billion) and is expected to fall to C$9.0 billion ($6.6 billion), or about one percent of gross domestic product, by fiscal 1998-99.
The Canadian dollar, bonds and T-bills strengthened after the budget update.
"Everybody is watching the Canada dollar because the strength of the dollar gives the (Bank of Canada) room to lower interest rates which is good for stocks," Ing said.
The currency ended firmer at C$1.3524 (US$0.7395) from Tuesday's close at C$1.3536 (US$0.7388).
On the TSE, eight of 14 groups ended higher led by banking, transport and conglomerates. The weak side included base metals, pipelines and energy.
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 506 to 428 with 287 issues ending flat.
* Inco Ltd. topped the active list, falling 0.50 to 39.90 on 2.7 million shares. Alcan Aluminum Ltd. sank 1 to 40.40. Both stocks were depressed by weak metal prices.

* Junior gold miner Bre-X Minerals Ltd. dropped 0.25 to 25.05 on 2.0 million shares. Reports last week of a dispute over its huge gold discovery in Indonesia continued to dog the high-flying stock, analysts said.
* Interest-rate sensitive stocks also moved ahead. Bank of Montreal gained 0.20 to 38.50, while Toronto-Dominion Bank improved 0.25 to 30.
Bank of Nova Scotia climbed 0.45 to a 52-week high of 40.15.

* Royal Plastics Group Ltd. jumped 1.05 to close at 25.65 on 485,000 shares. Royal Plastics earlier today acquired Rubbermaid Inc.'s 50-percent interest in a joint-owned company for an undisclosed price.
